segments.text: AI news in eighty seconds. Three verified updates, checked October third.
First, Black Forest Labs has released Flux Three Image.
The company describes images up to four K, targeted edits, and bounding boxes for placing objects.
Its demonstrations show changing part of a picture while preserving the rest. These are vendor claims.
Second, the Strands team has released Decider Two B, a small decision model with two billion parameters.
The official announcement says it can run locally on a processor or graphics card.
It chooses from supplied options or assigns scores, rather than writing free form text.
Code, weights, and training materials are available.
Third, U S Senators Josh Hawley and Chris Murphy announced the AI Agent Accountability Act.
The proposal would hold operators and developers responsible for certain hacking damage caused by AI agents.
The sponsors say developers could face liability for failing to add reasonable safeguards when they know of hacking capabilities.
This is proposed legislation, not an enacted law.
Read the original source links in the description for more details.
